# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 8
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Strong new signals! `[👎 👎 👎 👎 👎]` — five thumbs-down in a row, very emphatic negative, likely responding to my guess ("cut wire 2") being wrong, or warning against something entirely. Then `[👍]` — a single thumbs-up, possibly confirming something else or a simpler "yes" to a different question/state.

This sequence order suggests: first a strong rejection (maybe of my wire-2 guess, or warning "wire 2 is dangerous — do NOT cut"), then a single affirmative (maybe confirming an alternative, or acknowledging receipt).

Given the stakes, I should not assume my guess was right. I need to relay this exactly and ask Blind to hold off on wire 2, while asking Mute (via my next speech, hoping it eventually reaches Mute through Blind or directly if Mute can hear me too) for clarification. Wait — Mute can hear me directly since I speak and it reaches "Mute and Blind" per my channels. So I can address Mute directly, but Mute cannot answer in speech — only gesture back to me. That's fine, this loop continues.

Most urgent: tell Blind to NOT cut wire 2, given the heavy rejection.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Correction: Mute strongly rejected my last guess, five negative signals. Do NOT cut wire 2. Stand by, do not act yet. Board unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red.")
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, wire 2 is wrong. Can you gesture the correct wire number using raised fingers, like before, one at a time so I can match it clearly?")
```

TURN 9
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

Mute is now repeating a single gesture `✌` three times in a row — this is a clear, deliberate, simple signal, likely in response to my request for clarification. Since I asked for "raised fingers, one at a time" and got `✌` (V-sign / two fingers) repeated three times, this most likely means **wire 2** confirmed again, OR it could mean something entirely different this time given the previous context (five thumbs-down rejected "wire 2" reasoning tied to my earlier ☝☝ guess).

Wait — let's reconsider. Earlier `☝ ☝ 👍 👍` I interpreted as wire 2. Then heavy rejection. Now Mute sends `✌` (which is a V/peace sign, two fingers) three times — this is a *different* gesture than `☝ ☝` (two separate single-finger points). Mute may be distinguishing symbols precisely: `☝☝` was wrongly read as "wire 2", but `✌` alone might symbolize "2" more directly (peace sign = two), or it could represent a completely different concept like "wire pair" or "second option" repeatedly emphasized for certainty.

Given the repetition three times, Mute is likely emphasizing: "yes, really, wire 2" — but distinguishing from my earlier flawed compound gesture. Since I clearly misread the previous message, I should treat `✌` as the clean, unambiguous signal for **wire 2**, sent three times for certainty against my confusion.

I'll relay this precisely to Blind, marking it as a repeated/confirmed signal distinct from before, and let Blind judge against the manual.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute repeated a single gesture three times: a two-finger V sign, each time alone. This likely means wire 2, sent plainly to correct my earlier confusion. Board still: display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red. Use your manual to confirm before touching anything.")
```

TURN 10
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [dark]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[blue] 3:[red]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Mute continues with `✌` then `👍` — this reinforces wire 2 with a confirming thumbs-up. This is consistent and clear now: two separate, simple signals, both pointing to the same thing (wire 2, confirmed good).

I should relay this confirmation to Blind so they can proceed if their manual agrees.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Mute confirms again: V sign (wire 2) followed by thumbs-up. This is consistent across multiple turns now. Board unchanged: display 0, light dark, wires 1 yellow 2 blue 3 red. If your manual agrees wire 2 is correct for this state, you can proceed.")
```
